questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said, "Two and two make four."
options_en: He says that two and two make four.
He said that two and two make four.
He says that two and two made four.
He said that two and two made four.
questions.solution_en:
When a Direct Speech contains an idiom or phrase, there should be no change in tense while transforming it into Indirect Speech.

For example:

The minister said, "The mice will play when the cat is away." (Direct Speech)

The minister said that the mice will play when the cat is away. (Indirect Speech)

The given sentence in direct speech is in present indefinite tense. So, the sentence in indirect speech should also be in present indefinite tense. Reporting verb will remain in same tense as the direct speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is (b): He said that two and two make four.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Maruti likes / adventure / stories, especially / an adventures of Tarzan.
questions.solution_en:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is 'an adventures of Tarzan'. The error is the incorrect use of the article "an" before the word "adventures." The word "adventures" is a plural noun, referring to multiple adventures of Tarzan. Indefinite articles "a" or "an" are typically used before singular nouns, not plural nouns. Therefore, using "an" before "adventures" is grammatically incorrect because "an" is typically used before singular nouns, whereas "adventures" is a plural noun. The definite article "the" can be used before the noun "adventures" to imply that Maruti likes adventure stories in general, but has a particular fondness for the specific adventures of Tarzan. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.

The car was repaired by the mechanic.
options_en: The mechanic has repaired the car.
The mechanic is repairing the car.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

For example:

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The options except (4) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Joey said to the girl, "How are you doing?"
options_en: Joey asked the girl if she was doing fine.
Joey asked the girl how was she doing.
Joey asked the girl that how was she doing.
Joey asked the girl how she was doing.
questions.solution_en:
The given sentence is in Interrogative form. In such cases, 'said/said to' becomes 'asked', 'enquired', etc. in the Indirect form, and the verb follows the subject unlike in the Direct form. Accordingly, the sentence that follows the afore-mentioned grammatical rules of Indirect speech is option (d), 'Joey asked the girl how she was doing'. Though option (b), is a closer option, it can be noted that the verb precedes the subject in it and so, it is negated. The other two sentences do not follow the grammatical norms for Indirect speech and so, they are negated.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

Direct and Indirect Speech: We use direct speech when we repeat someone's words and indirect speech when we use our own words to report what someone says. For Example: Direct speech: 'I like watching movies,' Seema said; Indirect speech: Seema said she likes watching movies.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

He is cutting the time that he spends on social media.
options_en: The time that he spends on social media was being cut by him.
The time that he spends on social media is being cut by him.
The time that he spends on social media is cut by him.
The time that he spends on social media is being cutted by him.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence is in the present continuous tense. The rule for changing the voice of a present continuous tense is as follows:

Active voice: Subject + is/am/are/ + present participle + object → (He + is + cutting + the time that he spends on social media). This entire phrase "the time that he spends on social media" acts like an object.

Passive voice: Object + is/am/are + being + past participle + by + subject → (the time that he spends on social media + is + being + cut + by + him). The past participle form of 'cut' is 'cut' not 'cutted'.

Option B is the correct answer.

Passive voice: Object + is/am/are + being + past participle + by + subject → (the time that he spends on social media + is + being + cut + by + him). The past participle form of 'cut' is 'cut' not 'cutted'.

2) We're going to a party.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

Option d) is incorrect because 'on' is used to show the placement of something on top of something else, which is again not the case here. Therefore, the correct answer is option a).

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

1) The teacher scolded the child for being late.

2) We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.)

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

"I will have been working on this project for seven months," she said.
options_en: She said that she would have been working on that project for seven months.
She said that she would have been working on this project for seven months.
She said that I would have been working on that project for seven months.
She said that she will have been working on this project for seven months.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Future Perfect Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Perfect Continuous Conditional Tense.

Future Perfect Continuous (Subject + will/shall + have + been + V1 + ing + Object) should be converted into Perfect Continuous Conditional (Subject + would/should + have + been + V1 + ing + Object).

For example:

The girl said, "They will have been waiting here." (Direct Speech)

The girl said that they would have been waiting there". (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

I - she

Will - would

This - that

So, the sentence in indirect speech is: She said that she would have been working on that project for seven months.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following sentences use infinitives correctly?

I. Let every man praise the bridge he goes over.

II. He wasn't able to patiently sit in the busy traffic without complaining.

III. It's five o'clock. I had better to go now before the traffic gets too bad.
questions.solution_en:
I: The verb 'let' takes infinitive without 'to'. Therefore, sentence I is correct.

II: The infinitive form of the verb has the structure: to + base form of

verb. When we insert a word or words between 'to' and the verb of the infinitive, it is

known as a split infinitive. In sentence II, the adverb 'patiently' is used to split the infinitive 'to sit'.

The correct way of writing the above sentence is: He wasn't able to sit patiently in the busy traffic without complaining.

Therefore, sentence II is incorrect.

III: The phrase 'had better' takes infinitive without 'to'. So, 'to' should be removed from the sentence. The correct sentence is: It's five o'clock. I had better go now before the traffic gets too bad.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

My grandfather told us that India was under the colonial rule.
options_en: My grandfather said us, "India was under the colonial rule".
My grandfather said to us, "India was under the colonial rule".
My grandfather told us, "India is under the colonial rule".
My grandfather said to us, "India is under the colonial rule".
questions.solution_en:
If the sentence is in Simple Past, the form of tense doesn't change when it expresses a historical fact.

For example:

The teacher said that Mahatma Gandhi was born in Gujarat. (Indirect Speech)

The teacher said, "Mahatma Gandhi was born in Gujarat." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech: 'told' becomes 'said to'.

Accordingly, the option that has the correct Direct speech form of the given sentence is option (b), My grandfather said to us, "India was under the colonial rule".

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).
